CFML Language Reference: Functions

REReplace

Replaces the first match, or every match, of a regular expression with a replacement string.

Category

String functions

Syntax

REReplace(string, reg_expression, substring [, scope ])

Parameters

string
The string to work on.
reg_expression
The regular expression to search for. See REFind for the syntax.
substring
The replacement text. \1 to \9 insert the text matched by the corresponding parenthesized subexpression.
scope
Optional. "ONE" replaces only the first match (the default); "ALL" replaces every match.

Returns

The string with the replacements made.

Usage

Back references make it easy to rearrange text: REReplace(d, "([0-9]+)/([0-9]+)/([0-9]+)", "\3-\1-\2") turns 12/31/1999 into 1999-12-31.

As with Replace, the default scope is ONE. To strip all HTML tags from a string, use REReplace(text, "<[^>]*>", "", "ALL").

Example

Opens the example in a new window. The example runs on this server, so it only works when you browse from the server itself (127.0.0.1).
<CFSET Text = "Call 555-1234 or 555-9876, before 1/1/2000!">
<CFOUTPUT>
<P>Original: #Text#</P>
<UL>
<LI>Digits hidden: #REReplace(Text, "[[:digit:]]", "x", "ALL")#
<LI>First number swapped: #REReplace(Text, "([0-9]{3})-([0-9]{4})", "\2-\1")#
<LI>Date to ISO: #REReplace(Text, "([0-9]+)/([0-9]+)/([0-9]{4})", "\3-\1-\2")#
<LI>Tags stripped: #REReplace("<B>Bold</B> and <I>italic</I>", "<[^>]*>", "", "ALL")#
<LI>Spaces squeezed: #REReplace("too    many     spaces", "[[:space:]]+", " ", "ALL")#
</UL>
</CFOUTPUT>
